newsitem.title: USA: Clinton jumps to 20-point lead over Dole.
newsitem.headline: Clinton jumps to 20-point lead over Dole.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has jumped to a 20.1 percentage point lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole, up nearly six points from his three-day rolling average on Friday, the Reuters daily tracking poll showed on Saturday.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, showed Clinton with 49.9 percent and Dole with 29.8 percent, with 5 percent for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, 2.7 percent for other candidates and 12.6 percent undecided. On Friday, Clinton led Dole by 14.3 points.
"As the two candidates make final preparation for their debate in Hartford, Clinton's lead is just enormous, the largest we have seen in our polling to date," pollster John Zogby said.
He said Clinton's double digit lead could pave the way for bringing back Democratic majorities to the House and Senate.

The survey is based on responses of about 900 likely voters over a three day period. Each day, it creates a new rolling three-day average with a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percentage points.
